newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa urged to rethink state job severance pay.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa urged to rethink state job severance pay.

text.p: South Africa needs to rethink its programme of offering severance packages as a way of cutting the public service, Education Minister Sibusiso Bengu said on Monday.
"I do think we ought to rethink this matter of severance packages," Bengu told a parliamentary news briefing.
"One colleague of mine is describing it as 'shotgun' because you don't target the people that you want to leave. It just cuts across in a way that may be not wise," he said.
The government has set reducing the size of the civil service as one of its priorities, offering severance packages as an inducement for staff to leave voluntarily.
But the packages have been accepted by many people in senior positions, leaving several government departments short of trained and experienced personnel. Badly needed teachers have also quit.
"It may be time for it to be looked at again... not just within education but generally within government," Bengu said.
He said he hoped that despite plans for reduced government spending, education would receive more funding than last year in the budget to be presented by Finance Minister Trevor Manuel next month.
"We are involved in sensitive negotiations with finance," Bengu said.
"Our position is quite clear -- the education budget cannot be decreased because of the backlogs that are there... It is not the time for the government to decrease the education budget," he said.
